quotes.text: Depending on availability, you might have no recommendations or up to three at any given time.
Any estimated impacts, such as increases in revenue, are estimates and aren’t guaranteed.
Each recommendation includes an estimated impact, such as a revenue (otherwise known as payment volume) increase or fraud model improvement.
If you process all payments through Stripe, we handle this automatically.
Disabling 3DS won’t affect payments that require 3DS by regulation

old_evidence.text: Each recommendation includes an estimated impact, such as a revenue (otherwise known as payment volume) increase or fraud model improvement.
Depending on availability, you might have no recommendations or up to three at any given time.
If you process all payments through Stripe, we handle this automatically.

findings: The complete November guide and May guide describe Dashboard Acceptance-page suggestions, not automatic optimization actions: an account may show zero to three, based on settings, integration and thresholds; Stripe refreshes them daily and the merchant can dismiss or send feedback (old raw lines 8-20; new raw lines 9-21). Estimated impacts and recommendation outcomes are not guaranteed, may have cost/fraud/legal tradeoffs, and require business decision (old raw line 14; new raw line 15).

Both captures allow estimated revenue/payment-volume increase OR fraud-model improvement, with revenue increases displayed in settlement currency (old raw lines 22-26; new raw lines 23-27). Annualized revenue estimates use recent-month all or relevant volume multiplied by an average uplift and 12, assuming stable volume; the average comes from other businesses and relevant-volume estimates exclude inapplicable payments (old raw lines 28-34; new raw lines 29-33). Current source line 13 and related concept line 77 incorrectly imply each recommendation has an annual revenue estimate, so correct this baseline overstatement separately from the navigation/format delta.

The NTID recommendation applies to an off-session merchant-initiated transaction using a previous on-session transaction or validation from the same customer, especially when Stripe did not authorize the underlying card previously or card numbers are used without a Stripe Customer object. Stripe says it handles NTIDs automatically if all payments pass through Stripe; for other processors it might lack the ID unless supplied at PaymentIntent creation (old raw lines 36-45; new raw lines 35-44). Source line 26 should retain the same-customer, mixed-processor and automatic-handling conditions rather than implying every MIT requires a manual NTID.

Other recommendations remain: share postal codes for Visa credit AVS and potentially favorable US interchange; disable the two blunt AVS/CVC Radar blocks, optionally use risk-score variants while highest-risk automatic blocking remains; reduce manual 3DS requests on low-risk transactions outside regions with authentication requirements; investigate high 3DS abandonment (old raw lines 47-84; new raw lines 46-83). The source's five-row table broadly covers these at lines 22-35, but its 'SCA regions' shorthand must not imply all payments in a region require 3DS or that all fraud checks should be disabled (new raw lines 52-79).

Neither captured page specifies a recommendation acceptance API, observed authorization gain, processor settlement, actual fraud-model result or merchant-specific compliance decision. API versus Dashboard 3DS request controls are separate, and stopping optional requests does not affect payments that require 3DS by regulation (old raw lines 69-80; new raw lines 68-79). The linked guides and dashboard routes are navigation, not evidence of executed account changes.

The mapped source frontmatter lacks canonical_url (source lines 1-9), though the required source schema calls for the exact trusted URL (rules/ingest-roles.md lines 51-63). Add canonical_url: https://docs.stripe.com/payments/analytics/recommendations as a baseline metadata correction; this omission is independent of the presentation-only May-to-November raw diff (old raw line 1; new raw line 1; diff lines 1-67).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the May 8, 2026 raw provenance and the five types, zero-to-three account-dependent daily availability, estimation formulas and warnings as May evidence; the November capture repeats them without a substantive rule change (source lines 4-7, 13-35, 43-45; old raw lines 8-84; new raw lines 9-83).

Preserve the off-session MIT versus prior on-session same-customer NTID identity boundary, Stripe-only automatic handling versus mixed-processor possible missing ID, and PaymentIntent-creation condition with dated attribution (old raw lines 38-45; new raw lines 37-44).

Preserve the regulation-required 3DS exception and distinction between API manual request, Radar rule and Radar Authentication control; a recommendation to reduce optional 3DS is not proof that a particular payment needs no authentication (old raw lines 69-80; new raw lines 68-79).
conflicts: Current source line 13 and the existing concept at wiki/concepts/stripe-authorization-boost.md:77 state that each recommendation includes annual revenue impact; both old and new raw instead say estimated impact can be a revenue/payment-volume increase OR fraud-model improvement (old raw lines 22-26; new raw lines 23-27). Reciprocally qualify source and concept; annualization applies to applicable revenue estimates, not every recommendation.
unresolved_questions: The page does not say which recommendation types receive fraud-model estimates rather than annualized revenue estimates, or disclose the business-specific uplift values; account-specific recommendation presence and effect remain unobserved (new raw lines 11-33).

The page does not prove that changing Radar or 3DS settings improves a particular merchant's net revenue or fraud outcomes; its disclaimer explicitly leaves costs, risk and legal terms for the business to evaluate (new raw lines 15, 52-79).

findings: Add November raw provenance while retaining May ingestion and raw source history; the diff is heading whitespace and malformed-table layout cleanup, not a recommendation-policy change (source lines 4-7, 43-45; diff lines 1-67).

Add the missing canonical_url frontmatter field with the exact trusted identity https://docs.stripe.com/payments/analytics/recommendations (source lines 1-9; rules/ingest-roles.md lines 51-63; old raw line 1; new raw line 1). This is a pre-existing metadata omission, separate from the presentation-only raw diff.

Narrow source line 13: each recommendation has an estimated impact, but that may be revenue/payment volume or fraud-model improvement; annualized month × uplift × 12 applies to applicable revenue estimates with all-volume versus relevant-volume bases and stable-volume assumption (old raw lines 22-34; new raw lines 23-33). The related concept line 77 repeats the overstatement.
Qualify source line 26 NTID row with same-customer prior on-session ID, Stripe-only automatic handling and mixed-processor possible missing ID (old raw lines 38-45; new raw lines 37-44).

Make source lines 29 and 35 conditional: low-risk optional 3DS outside authentication-required regions may be reduced, while payments actually requiring 3DS by regulation remain subject to it (old raw lines 69-80; new raw lines 68-79).
conflicts: Source line 13 and concept line 77 promise annual revenue impact for every recommendation, conflicting with both captures' alternative fraud-model impact (old raw line 24; new raw line 25).
source_assessments.reason: No substantive new raw behavior is established, but the current source and concept materially overstate the impact type for every recommendation. Raw-reference provenance, the baseline impact correction and the missing canonical_url metadata correction are needed.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/analytics/recommendations, the complete November guide describes account-dependent Dashboard Acceptance recommendations: zero to three can appear, they refresh daily, and the merchant decides whether to act after considering uncertain estimates, costs, fraud and legal terms (new raw lines 9-21). Impacts can be revenue/payment-volume increases or fraud-model improvement; applicable revenue estimates annualize recent all or relevant monthly volume using an average uplift and a stable-volume assumption (new raw lines 23-33). The five topics are same-customer NTID for off-session MIT, Visa postal AVS, Radar rule changes, lower optional 3DS and 3DS integration diagnosis (new raw lines 35-83). The May capture documents the same boundaries (old raw lines 8-84). source-stripe-payments-recommendations.md captures the five recommendations but line 13 overstates that each has annual revenue impact, line 26 compresses same-customer and processor conditions, and frontmatter lines 1-9 omit the required canonical URL identity. A recommendation is a suggestion, not an executed account change or guaranteed authorization outcome.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/analytics/recommendations, the diff shows presentation cleanup of whitespace and an awkward impact table, with no substantive recommendation or eligibility rule change (old raw lines 16-34, 36-84; new raw lines 17-33, 35-83). source-stripe-payments-recommendations.md should retain May-dated claims, add November provenance, and add its missing canonical_url frontmatter field using this trusted URL (source lines 1-9; old raw line 1; new raw line 1). That metadata omission is pre-existing and separate from the raw diff. Its baseline annual-revenue-for-every-item overstatement at line 13 also needs correction; the related concept line 77 needs a reciprocal qualifier because fraud-model impacts are possible. The NTID advice is off-session MIT tied to an earlier on-session transaction or validation from the same customer, with Stripe-only automatic handling and mixed-processor caveats (old raw lines 38-45; new raw lines 37-44). Radar rules, Dashboard controls and API-requested 3DS are distinct surfaces. Disabling optional 3DS does not override a payment's regulatory requirement, and a forecast, feedback action or recommendation display cannot establish real revenue, fraud improvement, authorization or settlement.
